notes: The circuit image draws the wires and the two 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistors without showing a breadboard. I used one mini breadboard (bb1) as the junction for the pull-ups and the SDA/SCL joins. The parts list names 2 mini breadboards, but only one is needed, so a second one is not included.

The image shows the reader's pin labelled '3V'. I mapped it to the catalogue port 3V3 on the Nano 33 IoT. The wire from there feeds the pull-up resistors only, because the writer's 3V3 pin is not connected.

In the image, SDA (yellow) joins reader A4 and writer A4, and SCL (teal) joins reader A5 and writer A5. One 4.7 kΩ resistor pulls each line up to 3V3. The teal and yellow lines cross in the drawing, but the small hop shows they are not connected at the crossing.
The 3V3 rail sits on the top positive rail of the breadboard, with the resistor ends at tp.3 and tp.6. These hole positions are arbitrary because the image doesn't specify them.
Both boards are powered and programmed over USB cables from the computer. The usb-cable catalogue entry has no ports, so those edges name only the Nano's USB port.
GND is a single jumper wire between the two boards' GND pins. I used GND.1 on both as an assumption.
The reader/writer sketches and the Serial Monitor screenshot don't add any parts or connections.
